newsitem.title: UK: Non-OPEC Oct supply jump sets tone for Q4 - IEA.
newsitem.headline: Non-OPEC Oct supply jump sets tone for Q4 - IEA.

text.p: Oil supply from outside OPEC leapt by 830,000 barrels per day (bpd) in October to 44.2 million bpd and should average 45 million over the fourth quarter, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.

Despite a sharp downward revision to its September estimate -- the Paris-based agency said non-OPEC supply rose 445,000 bpd against the 800,000 bpd anticipated -- the IEA believe its October forecast will stand.
"There is some evidence that the period of downward revisions in non-OPEC supply estimates may be coming to an end," it said in its latest monthly report.

"New field start-ups in the North Sea, Brazil, the Gulf of Mexico and elsewhere are beginning to offer more positive than negative surprises and technical difficulties in the U.K. Forties system, offshore Australia and in Alaska may have now been fully factored into the forecasts."
The largest growth was seen in U.K. offshore output which climbed 370,000 bpd, boosted by four new fields which started up in late September and during last month.

"October developments appear to have a much more positive tone with production increasing to 3.0 million bpd, setting the stage for the expected rally in U.K. production in fourth quarter 1996," the IEA said.
Norwegian production was stable at just below 3.2 million bpd, failing to meet expectations due to maintenance programmes that were more extensive than expected.

The IEA also pointed to higher output offshore China following a weather-related decline in September and a sustained recovery in Mexican production, which together added a total of 200,000 bpd of incremental supply.

"Afer the seemingly uninterrupted series of downward revisions in supply, which started a year ago with the Gulf of Mexico hurricanes and an unexpectedly slow start-up of the Norwegian Heidrun field, this month may represent a watershed," the IEA said.
North American production gained 100,000 bpd in October but Russian output is estimated to have fallen 30,000 bpd, extending September's losses of 85,000 bpd.
